title: Conjecture 6.1
context_text: For a $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ and $0\le i<k$, the $i$-skeleton $H^{(i)}$ is the $(i+1)$-uniform hypergraph on $V(H)$ whose edges are all $(i+1)$-sets contained in some edge of $H$, and the $i$-th skeletal degeneracy $d_i(H)$ is the degeneracy of $H^{(i)}$ (the least $d$ such that every subhypergraph of $H^{(i)}$ has minimum degree at most $d$); thus $d_1(H)$, the skeletal degeneracy, is the degeneracy of the graph obtained by replacing every edge of $H$ by a clique, and $d_{k-1}(H)$ is the usual degeneracy of $H$. The $q$-color Ramsey number $r(H;q)$ is the least $N$ such that every $q$-coloring of the edges of the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph $K^{(k)}_N$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$, and $\exp^{(k)}(x)$ is the exponential tower of height $k$ with $x$ on top: $\exp^{(1)}(x)=2^x$, $\exp^{(k)}(x)=2^{\exp^{(k-1)}(x)}$. Answering a question of Conlon, Fox and Sudakov (a hypergraph analogue of the Burr–Erdős conjecture proved by Lee), the authors prove that $k$-uniform hypergraphs with bounded skeletal degeneracy have linear Ramsey number; for $k\ge4$ their proof gives $r(H;q)\le\exp^{(k-1)}(O_{k,q}(d))n$ with $d=d_1(H)$, which is generally expected to be best possible. For $k=3$ it only gives $r(H;q)\le\exp^{(2)}(O_q(d\log d))n$, improved to $\exp^{(2)}(O_q(d))n$ when the 1-skeleton $H^{(1)}$ has bounded chromatic number; the conjecture is that the $\log d$ factor can always be removed. A similar statement is known (Bradač, Fox, Sudakov) with $d_1(H)$ replaced by the square root of the number of edges, and the conjecture would be stronger since $d_1(H)\le O(\sqrt{e(H)})$.
paper_title: Ramsey and Turán numbers of sparse hypergraphs

title: Conjecture 6.2
statement_text: There is a constant $c_{k}>0$ such that for every $k$-uniform $k$-partite hypergraph $H$, $\mathrm{ex}(n,H)\leq O_{H}\left(n^{k-\frac{c_{k}}{d_{\mathsf{max}}(H)}}\right).$
context_text: For a $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ and $0\le i<k$, the $i$-skeleton $H^{(i)}$ is the $(i+1)$-uniform hypergraph on $V(H)$ whose edges are all $(i+1)$-sets contained in some edge of $H$, and the $i$-th skeletal degeneracy $d_i(H)$ is the degeneracy of $H^{(i)}$ (the least $d$ such that every subhypergraph of $H^{(i)}$ has minimum degree at most $d$); thus $d_1(H)$, the skeletal degeneracy, is the degeneracy of the graph obtained by replacing every edge of $H$ by a clique, and $d_{k-1}(H)$ is the usual degeneracy of $H$. The Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(n,H)$ is the maximum number of edges of an $H$-free $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. The authors prove that for every $k$-uniform $k$-partite $H$ with at least two edges, $\Omega_k(n^{k-C_k/d_1(H)})\le\mathrm{ex}(n,H)\le O_H(n^{k-c_k/d_1(H)^{k-1}})$; the upper bound is tight in terms of $d_1$ for the complete $k$-partite $k$-uniform hypergraph $K^{(k)}_{d,\dots,d}$, and the lower bound is tight for the bipartite hedgehog $H^{(k)}_d$ (each edge of $K_{d,d}$ extended to a $k$-edge by $k-2$ new vertices), so $d_1$ alone does not determine the Turán exponent. With $d_{\mathsf{max}}(H)=\max_{1\le i<k}d_i(H)$, one has $d_1(H)\le d_{\mathsf{max}}(H)\le d_1(H)^{k-1}$, and the authors prove $\mathrm{ex}(n,H)\ge\Omega_k(n^{k-C_k/d_{\mathsf{max}}(H)})$ for every $k$-partite $H$ with at least two edges. The conjecture states that this lower bound is tight up to the constant, i.e. that $d_{\mathsf{max}}(H)$ controls the Turán exponent of $k$-partite $k$-uniform hypergraphs, as degeneracy is conjectured to do for bipartite graphs (Erdős's conjecture $\mathrm{ex}(n,H)=O(n^{2-1/d})$ for $d$-degenerate bipartite $H$).

title: Conjecture 6.4
statement_text: Let $L$ be a $d\times d$ Latin square. Define $H_{L}$ to be the 3-uniform 3-partite hypergraph on vertex set $[d]\sqcup[d]\sqcup[d]$ where $(i,j,k)\in E(H_{L})$ if and only if $L(i,j)=k$. Then $\mathrm{ex}(n,H_{L})=n^{3-\Theta(1/d)}$.
context_text: For a $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ and $0\le i<k$, the $i$-skeleton $H^{(i)}$ is the $(i+1)$-uniform hypergraph on $V(H)$ whose edges are all $(i+1)$-sets contained in some edge of $H$, and the $i$-th skeletal degeneracy $d_i(H)$ is the degeneracy of $H^{(i)}$ (the least $d$ such that every subhypergraph of $H^{(i)}$ has minimum degree at most $d$); thus $d_1(H)$, the skeletal degeneracy, is the degeneracy of the graph obtained by replacing every edge of $H$ by a clique, and $d_{k-1}(H)$ is the usual degeneracy of $H$. The Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(n,H)$ is the maximum number of edges of an $H$-free 3-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. A $d\times d$ Latin square $L$ is a $d\times d$ array filled with symbols from $[d]$ such that each symbol occurs exactly once in each row and each column. The authors prove $\mathrm{ex}(n,H)\le O_H(n^{3-c/d_1(H)^2})$ for every 3-partite 3-uniform $H$, and conjecture that in general $\mathrm{ex}(n,H)\le O_H(n^{k-c_k/d_{\mathsf{max}}(H)})$ for $k$-partite $k$-uniform $H$, where $d_{\mathsf{max}}(H)=\max_{1\le i<k}d_i(H)$; a matching lower bound $\Omega(n^{k-C_k/d_{\mathsf{max}}(H)})$ is proved. The hardest cases should be those with a large gap between $d_{\mathsf{max}}(H)$ and $d_1(H)^{k-1}$, and Latin squares give such an example: $d_1(H_L),d_2(H_L)=\Theta(d)$, yet their theorem only gives $\mathrm{ex}(n,H_L)\le O(n^{3-c/d^2})$. Indeed the 1-skeleton of $H_L$ is $K_{d,d,d}$, the same as that of the complete 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraph $K^{(3)}_{d,d,d}$, and their techniques find $H_L$ only by finding the much larger $K^{(3)}_{d,d,d}$, which contains every 3-partite hypergraph with at most $d$ vertices in each part.

title: Conjecture 6.5
statement_text: There is a constant $c>0$ such that for all $d\geq 4$ the following holds. If $G$ is a (not necessarily linear) 3-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with at least $n^{3-c/d}$ edges, then there is a linear subhypergraph of $G$ with $d$ vertices and at least $d^{2}/100$ edges.
context_text: A hypergraph is linear if any two of its edges share at most one vertex; a subhypergraph of $G$ on $d$ vertices is a set of $d$ vertices together with some of the edges of $G$ inside it. For a $d\times d$ Latin square $L$ (each symbol of $[d]$ once in each row and each column), $H_L$ is the 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraph on $[d]\sqcup[d]\sqcup[d]$ with edges $(i,j,k)$ such that $L(i,j)=k$; it is linear, with $3d$ vertices and $d^2$ edges. The authors conjecture that $\mathrm{ex}(n,H_L)=n^{3-\Theta(1/d)}$, where $\mathrm{ex}(n,H)$ is the maximum number of edges of an $H$-free 3-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices, but their methods only find $H_L$ in hypergraphs with $n^{3-c/d^2}$ edges, by finding the complete 3-partite hypergraph $K^{(3)}_{d,d,d}$, which is far from linear. They suggest it would still be interesting to find some Latin square (not a specific one), or even some large part of one, in any hypergraph of density $n^{3-c/d}$, and propose this weaker conjecture, which they are still unable to prove. Without the linearity requirement it is easy: a hypergraph generalization of the Kővári–Sós–Turán argument (Erdős) shows that every 3-uniform hypergraph with at least $n^{3-c/d}$ edges contains $K^{(3)}_{1,(d-1)/2,(d-1)/2}$, a non-linear hypergraph with $d$ vertices and $(d-1)^2/4$ edges.
paper_title: Ramsey and Turán numbers of sparse hypergraphs
